problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation  $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-0.7,$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$   are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$, $\,x≈$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.7)=-44.427\,004{…}^{∘}≈-{44.4270}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $x=-{44.4270}^{∘}$ is not in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ To get the first solution that's within the required domain, we need to find an angle that's coterminal with $-{44.4270}^{∘}.$ To do this, we simply add ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{44.4270}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={315.5730}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={44.4270}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={44.4270}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977985/assets/f3d2d41e1a58dd562ed47ae7e5fcdc79382c426700f520a1153111bfcf2d734b.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{44.4270}^{∘} \\  & ={224.4270}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈{224.4}^{∘},\,x≈{315.6}^{∘}.
$$
